neighbours.label: the modal ' may' (and weakly ' must') in a clause describing how a symptom or effect behaves over time (a pain that may last, swelling that may spread), as against the same clause with a plain verb
fire: After the injection, a dull ache that may persist for a day is normal.
Some people get a rash on the arms that may spread to the chest.
Patients often notice a burning feeling that may come and go for weeks.
A jellyfish sting leaves a red welt that may itch for several hours.
The surgery can leave a numbness in the fingers that may take months to fade.
Many runners describe a stitch in the side that may return on long hills.
Children with the virus develop a fever that may rise sharply at night.
Sunburn produces a tightness of the skin that may linger after the redness goes.
